extracted.intended_audience: NSF program officers, external reviewers, and proposers (principal investigators) involved in NSF merit review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for NSF proposal merit review: the two merit review criteria, special funding mechanisms (EAGER/RAPID/RAISE), reviewer selection and conflict-of-interest rules, review methods, program officer responsibilities, and reconsideration/oversight procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Intellectual Merit criterion encompasses the potential to advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must separately address Intellectual Merit in the Project Summary; failure to do so can result in the proposal being returned without review (RWR). Programs may elaborate additional elements to be considered; the Intellectual Merit assessment is a principal basis for reviewer evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Broader Impacts criterion encompasses the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must separately address Broader Impacts in the Project Summary; failure to do so can result in return without review. Examples of Broader Impacts considerations include integration of research and education and broadening participation. Programs may specify additional review criteria in solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RAISE eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: RAISE proposals support bold, interdisciplinary projects whose: (1) scientific advances lie largely outside the scope of a single program/discipline requiring substantial support from more than one program or discipline; (2) lines of research promise transformational advances; and (3) prospective discoveries reside at disciplinary interfaces that may not be recognized through traditional review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three RAISE criteria must be met for a project to be considered RAISE-appropriate. RAISE was introduced to encourage transformative interdisciplinary research; solicitations provide additional program-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: EAGER eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: EArly-concept Grants for Exploratory Research (EAGER) support exploratory work in its early stages on untested but potentially transformative research ideas or approaches (often high-risk/high-payoff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EAGER work may involve radically different approaches, new expertise, or novel disciplinary perspectives. Requests may be for up to $300,000 and up to two years. EAGER proposals are commonly reviewed using internal reviewers; program officers may choose to obtain external reviews and must inform the PI if external review will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: RAPID eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants for Rapid Response Research (RAPID) support proposals requiring severe urgency regarding availability of, or access to, data, facilities, or specialized equipment (e.g., quick-response research on natural or anthropogenic disasters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RAPID requests may be for up to $200,000 and of one year duration. RAPID proposals are commonly reviewed internally; program officers may elect external review and must inform the PI if so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals Returned Without Review (RWR) grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF returns proposals without review under several circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common RWR reasons include: failure to separately address both merit review criteria within the Project Summary (effective FY2003), duplication of an existing award, non-responsiveness to the funding opportunity, non-compliance with PAPPG or specific solicitation requirements, and other regulatory noncompliance. NSF has improved pre-submission electronic checks to reduce RWRs. See program-specific guidance for additional RWR categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for selecting ad hoc reviewers and/or panel members to ensure proper expertise to evaluate proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimal reviewer characteristics include: (1) special knowledge of the science/engineering subfields involved to evaluate competence and intellectual merit; (2) broader/generalized knowledge to evaluate broader impacts, especially for large, complex, multidisciplinary, or nationally/internationally significant proposals; (3) broad knowledge of the science and engineering enterprise infrastructure and educational activities to evaluate societal contributions and resource distribution; and (4) diverse representation within the review group (considering organization type, demographics, experience, and geographic balance). Selection should minimize conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest checks and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers check for conflicts of interest and instruct reviewers on identifying and declaring potential conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All NSF program officers and division directors receive annual conflict-of-interest training. Reviewers are expected to declare potential conflicts; program officers should select reviewers with no apparent conflicts. COI processes are integral to reviewer selection and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum review expectations and review methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals usually receive at least three external reviews; the principal review methods are ad hoc-only, panel-only, and ad hoc + panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad hoc-only: reviewers submit individual written reviews. Panel-only: convened panelists discuss and advise as a group. Ad hoc + panel: hybrid configurations (e.g., ad hoc reviews before panel or ad hoc supplements after panel) that often yield the largest number of written reviews (ad hoc+panel averaged 4.8 reviews/proposal in FY2018). Choice of method affects time-to-decision and matching of expertise: panel-only tends to reduce processing time; ad hoc permits more precise expertise matching; ad hoc+panel combines depth and comparative analysis. Under certain circumstances (e.g., EAGER, RAPID, RAISE, some workshops) external review requirements can be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officer responsibilities in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Program officers have specified responsibilities throughout the merit review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include: determining appropriate level/method of merit review; selecting ad hoc reviewers and/or panelists per NSF guidelines; checking for conflicts of interest; synthesizing reviewer and panel comments; and recommending award or decline after scientific, technical, and programmatic review and considering factors such as portfolio balance and funding availability. Division directors and other officials review program officer recommendations; large awards may receive additional levels of review (Director’s Review Board, NSB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program officer portfolio considerations beyond reviewer ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: When making funding recommendations, program officers weigh reviewer ratings/comments and consider additional portfolio and programmatic factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considerations include: support for high-risk proposals with potential for transformative advances; funding different approaches to significant research and education questions; capacity-building in new research areas; potential impact on human resources and infrastructure; NSF core strategies (integration of research and education; broadening participation); achievement of special program objectives/initiatives; availability of other funding resources; and geographic distribution. Program officers may fund risky proposals via small 'proof of concept' awards and consider broader impacts not apparent to reviewers. Decisions are made in the context of other current proposals and previously funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration process and permissible grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Declined proposers may request formal reconsideration under defined circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reconsideration request may be based on perceived procedural errors or disagreements over substantive issues raised by reviewers. Information about the reconsideration process is included in decline notifications. If the Assistant Director/Office Head upholds the original action, the proposer's institution may request a second reconsideration from the Deputy Director (or Chief Operating Officer if no Deputy Director). Certain types of proposal actions are not eligible for reconsideration per PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of panel discussions and advantages
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel discussions integrate different perspectives and can identify proposal strengths and weaknesses that individual written reviews may miss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels often provide broader perspectives; panel summaries may represent review perspectives larger than written reviews alone. The use of panels has increased and, by enabling comparative analysis, can affect ratings and processing times. Panel participation workload is higher and can affect willingness to serve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of site visits for facilities and centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Site visits (on-site and reverse-site) are used to review proposals for facilities and centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site visits typically involve NSF staff and external community members and are an additional review method for evaluating large-scale infrastructure and center proposals. Program officers have discretion in using site visits, subject to approval by division directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: External oversight and periodic assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: External oversight mechanisms assess the integrity and efficiency of the merit review process and program structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every 4–5 years, Committees of Visitors (COVs) examine major NSF programs/divisions. COV reports and NSF responses are publicly available. Directorate and Office Advisory Committees review COV reports and provide guidance. NSB and Director-level boards review large awards and programmatic matters to ensure accountability and adherence to policy.
